scientific_review: All111 identities and previous342 qualified depth references retained, including three audited datum normalizations. Bjørnøya adds a source-reported approximately580m maximum depth of a static Atlantic-Water velocity-ranked half-transport core.343 references,101 direct owners,10 without own refs; no full-route physical depth profile or whole-current volume estimate.

Original source Figure3d pixels on PDF5/printed21 were viewed to qualitatively corroborate the source prose mask depth. No figure digitization. Published1993–2022 hydrographic/altimetry mean retains53 Bjørnøya transects and irregular seasonal sampling.50m is a source surface exclusion, not a physical upper boundary; no quarterly mask-depth time series is created from interpolated property series.

Svinøy460m/approximately11km2,Gimsøy530m/approximately8km2 andBjørnøya580m/approximately17km2 are explicitly paired through immutable section-owned references and the same source static-mean transport-ranked AW core definition. Existing Svinøy/Gimsøy depth rows are not rewritten. Their1500/2500m lateral cutoffs are not inherited at Bjørnøya. BSO has a salinity-ranked core and is excluded.

The tenth profile uses Gimsøy andBjørnøya only, on the source’s approximate750km inter-section pathway. It interpolates maximum core-mask depth and cross-sectional area in that abstract distance coordinate. No geographical axis, exact endpoint longitude, OSW route distance, full-current length or georeferenced polygon is invented. All previous nine profiles and their CSV quantity cells remain unchanged.

A second provisional regional core-volume scenario integrates the source8 and17km2 mask areas with linear area change over750km. Computed trapezoid9375km3 is displayed at coarse precision as approximately9000km3. Area-times-distance units give cubic kilometres. Maximum depths are descriptive companions, not uniform thicknesses or rectangle factors.

The paper’s heat-budget box separately sets50km width,10km2 section area,200m depth and7500km3 volume. Those idealized box values are retained as context and are not used as actual core geometry, substituted into the integral, or treated as uncertainty bounds around the regional scenario.

Source midpoint-cell rectangles slightly overestimate area by neglecting topographic partial-cell cuts. This bias is retained qualitatively without an invented correction or confidence interval. The source path length and section areas are approximate. Section areas are assumed normal to the abstract pathway for extrusion; map geometry and orientation corrections are not recovered.

Extrusion of a static1993–2022 mean-core geometry is neither a dated observed volume nor a mean of instantaneous core volumes. Broad NwASC continuation may overlap modern West Spitsbergen naming; no independent additive component volume, physical-state allocation or global total is admitted. The prior EAC regional reference-geometry record remains exact, giving two separate qualified regional scenarios.

Seventy-two cloud checks include seven new depth-source tests, all57 previous profile tests and eight new matched-geometry/volume tests. Six baseline checks also pass:78 total. Checks cover source ownership, periods, section/mask/area mismatches, source-box confusion, invalid geometry substitutions, previous JSON/CSV preservation, distinct path coordinates and non-admission to whole-current/seasonal/physical-state/global products.

Local work was small metadata generation and original-document inspection on one idle CPU. Tests ran in cloud. No new ocean-field processing, local tests, runtime/WASM/browser/server execution or UI integration.
